caption:
Both show up well in interviews. They prove different things.

Open source proves you can read a big codebase you didn't write, take review comments, and get a change merged by strangers. That's most of the first year of a job. The catch: your first merged PRs are usually small, and finding a good first issue takes time.

Your own project proves you can design something, ship it, and explain every decision. The catch: nobody reviews it, so bad habits survive.

If you've done either, what did interviewers actually ask you about it?
